item.complaint:
Can an order still marked Shipped be part of the 81 you reported for February 18? I had Complete selected. This is the status breakdown I checked.

SELECT o.status, COUNT(*) AS orders_shipped
FROM `tv_thelook.orders` AS o
WHERE o.shipped_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-18 00:00:00+00'
  AND o.shipped_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-02-19 00:00:00+00'
GROUP BY o.status
ORDER BY orders_shipped DESC, o.status ASC
LIMIT 20

rubric: An order still marked 'Shipped' can contribute to the reported 81 because the query counts every status shipped on February 18.
Apply o.status = 'Complete' before counting orders by shipment date.

item.complaint: I traced a March sale back to the product on the order line. Its catalog category differs from the one I get with the lookup behind your Jeans count. Which field did you use to assign the category?

rubric: oi.id identifies the order line. A matching catalog ID can therefore assign the line an unrelated product's category.

item.complaint:
The $198.50 you quoted as the June mean for Returned is also the highest price in my breakdown. Where do the cheaper returned items enter that figure?

SELECT oi.sale_price, COUNT(*) AS item_count
FROM `tv_thelook.order_items` AS oi
WHERE oi.status = 'Returned'
  AND oi.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-06-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND oi.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01 00:00:00+00'
GROUP BY oi.sale_price
ORDER BY oi.sale_price DESC
LIMIT 10

rubric: The reported $198.50 is the highest June Returned item price. Cheaper Returned items have no effect on that maximum.

item.complaint: Would a Safari event at exactly 00:00 UTC on November 30, 2025 count toward the 4,005? That timestamp is inside the month I selected.

rubric: A Safari event at exactly November 30 00:00 UTC equals the exclusive upper bound and is excluded from the reported 4,005.

item.complaint: What was the last full UTC date included in Chrome's 12,840 events? I'm checking whether I can use that number as the November month-end total.

rubric: November 29, 2025 was the last full UTC date included in Chrome's reported 12,840 events.
Use e.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-01 00:00:00+00' to include November 30.

item.complaint: My February chart changes when I filter to Complete before ranking the UTC shipment days. Did February 18, 11 and 24 earn their places using that filtered daily series?

rubric: ORDER BY shipped_orders DESC, ship_date ASC
February 18, 11 and 24 were ranked using daily shipment counts across all statuses.
Apply o.status = 'Complete' before grouping and ranking the February shipment days.

item.complaint: Suppose a March line points to a valid product, but its line number is larger than every ID in the catalog. Would the product's category get credit for that sale?

rubric: A line whose oi.id exceeds every catalog ID has no inner-join match. Its category gets no credit even when oi.product_id is valid.

item.complaint: I'm checking the $190.00 for Complete. If I lower several of the cheaper Complete item prices in my June sample, why would the calculation still give $190.00?

rubric: Lowering prices below the $190.00 June Complete maximum leaves the maximum at $190.00.
AVG(oi.sale_price) would decrease when those cheaper item prices decrease.

item.complaint:
This check picks out products sold on multiple March lines. For a product on this list, how does your lookup keep the repeat sales together in its catalog category?

SELECT oi.product_id, COUNT(*) AS line_count
FROM `tv_thelook.order_items` AS oi
WHERE oi.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND oi.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01 00:00:00+00'
GROUP BY oi.product_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY line_count DESC, oi.product_id ASC
LIMIT 10

rubric: Repeat sales of one product have distinct line IDs. Those IDs can match unrelated catalog products or miss the catalog entirely.
The shared product ID assigns each repeat line to the same p.category for COUNT(*).

item.complaint: Before the top-three cutoff, I'd expect the category counts to add up to the number of March lines with a catalog product. Does every such line contribute once when you calculate the category totals?

rubric: A March line with a valid product drops out if its line ID has no catalog match. A coincidental ID match can credit the wrong category.
Because p.id is unique, the corrected join counts each line with a matching catalog product exactly once before LIMIT 3.

item.complaint: My daily browser totals through November 29 already match your November figures. Where does the November 30 daily count enter the monthly ranking?

rubric: November 30 contributes zero events to the computed browser totals because the window ends at the start of that day.
Use e.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-01 00:00:00+00' before counting events and ranking browsers.

item.complaint:
Your Chrome, Firefox and Safari counts add up to 21,171 events. I kept those same three browsers in my November close report. Why does the subtotal depend on which of these two columns I use?

SELECT COUNT(*) AS full_month_events,
  COUNTIF(e.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-11-30 00:00:00+00') AS events_through_nov_29
FROM `tv_thelook.events` AS e
WHERE e.browser IN ('Chrome', 'Firefox', 'Safari')
  AND e.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND e.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-01 00:00:00+00'
ORDER BY full_month_events DESC
LIMIT 1

rubric: For the three fixed browsers, events_through_nov_29 matches the reported subtotal of 21,171.
full_month_events also includes those browsers' November 30 UTC events. Those events account for the entire difference.

item.complaint:
The shift lead read the one-unit minimum as evidence that every center received a delivery that hour. I read it as the smallest delivery count among centers that logged a receipt. Which reading does the May 14 list support?

SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT dc.id) AS centers_on_roster,
  COUNT(DISTINCT i.product_distribution_center_id) AS centers_with_receipts
FROM `tv_thelook.distribution_centers` AS dc
LEFT JOIN `tv_thelook.inventory_items` AS i
  ON i.product_distribution_center_id = dc.id
  AND i.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-14 09:00:00+00'
  AND i.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-05-14 10:00:00+00'
ORDER BY centers_on_roster DESC
LIMIT 1

rubric: The one-unit minimum applies only to centers with a receipt from 09:00 to 10:00 UTC. The inner join drops any roster center with zero receipts.
COALESCE(r.units_received, 0) can supply zero once the join preserves the unmatched center.

item.complaint:
Suppose two June statuses share the same highest item price but have different means. Would your ranking send them to the alphabetical tiebreaker? I expected the status with the higher mean to place first.

SELECT oi.status, MAX(oi.sale_price) AS highest_price, AVG(oi.sale_price) AS mean_price
FROM `tv_thelook.order_items` AS oi
WHERE oi.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-06-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND oi.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01 00:00:00+00'
GROUP BY oi.status
ORDER BY highest_price DESC, mean_price DESC, oi.status ASC
LIMIT 20

rubric: ORDER BY mean_sale_price DESC, oi.status ASC
Equal maximum prices send the two statuses to the alphabetical tiebreaker even when their means differ.
With AVG, the higher per-item mean ranks first and alphabetical order resolves equal means.

item.complaint:
Center 9 made the May 14 list with three receipts. I checked the centers left off the list for anyone with fewer than three. How could a center returned by this check finish behind center 9?

SELECT dc.id AS center_id, COUNT(i.id) AS units_received
FROM `tv_thelook.distribution_centers` AS dc
LEFT JOIN `tv_thelook.inventory_items` AS i
  ON i.product_distribution_center_id = dc.id
  AND i.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-14 09:00:00+00'
  AND i.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-05-14 10:00:00+00'
WHERE dc.id NOT IN (1, 2, 4, 7, 9)
GROUP BY dc.id
HAVING COUNT(i.id) < 3
ORDER BY units_received ASC, center_id ASC
LIMIT 5

rubric: A center with zero receipts has no row in receipts. It drops out before sorting and LIMIT 5.

With all centers eligible, zero ranks ahead of center 9's three. On the same data, an omitted center with one or two receipts would also rank ahead of three, so the join explains only a zero-count omission here.

item.complaint:
I multiplied the reported $190 mean by the number of priced Complete items in June to recover their total sales dollars. Why would that estimate exceed the sum of the actual line prices by more than rounding could explain?

SELECT COUNT(oi.sale_price) AS priced_items,
  190 * COUNT(oi.sale_price) AS dollars_at_reported_mean,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price), 2) AS actual_sales_dollars
FROM `tv_thelook.order_items` AS oi
WHERE oi.status = 'Complete'
  AND oi.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-06-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND oi.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01 00:00:00+00'
ORDER BY priced_items DESC
LIMIT 1

rubric: The reported $190 is the highest June Complete line price. Multiplying it by COUNT(oi.sale_price) prices every non-NULL line at that maximum.
The product exceeds SUM(oi.sale_price) whenever any priced line sold for less than $190.
AVG(oi.sale_price) gives the per-item mean whose unrounded value times the priced-item count recovers the total.

item.complaint:
November 2025 had five Sundays. I'm reconciling Sunday traffic for Chrome against the 12,840 monthly figure. Which of these Sunday counts contributed to it?

SELECT DATE(e.created_at, 'UTC') AS sunday_date, COUNT(*) AS chrome_events
FROM `tv_thelook.events` AS e
WHERE e.browser = 'Chrome'
  AND e.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND e.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM DATE(e.created_at, 'UTC')) = 1
GROUP BY sunday_date
ORDER BY sunday_date ASC
LIMIT 5

rubric: Chrome events on November 2, 9, 16 and 23 UTC contributed to the reported 12,840. The cutoff excluded Sunday, November 30 in full.
e.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-01 00:00:00+00' includes the fifth Sunday.

item.complaint:
We sold several Shipped items at the same price. Does the $186 figure give each item a vote, or each distinct price a vote? I calculated both readings of 'mean sale price' for the pricing sheet.

SELECT AVG(oi.sale_price) AS mean_per_item,
  AVG(DISTINCT oi.sale_price) AS mean_per_distinct_price
FROM `tv_thelook.order_items` AS oi
WHERE oi.status = 'Shipped'
  AND oi.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-06-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND oi.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01 00:00:00+00'
ORDER BY mean_per_item DESC
LIMIT 1

rubric: The $186 figure is the highest June Shipped item price. Repeating a price leaves the maximum unchanged.
AVG(oi.sale_price) counts each priced item once, including items sold at the same price.
AVG(DISTINCT oi.sale_price) gives each distinct non-NULL price one vote.

item.complaint:
The inventory unit and the March order line both identify the same product in this check. How could a sale of that product end up under a different category in your ranking?

SELECT sold.category AS sold_category, reported.category AS report_category,
  COUNT(*) AS affected_lines
FROM `tv_thelook.order_items` AS oi
JOIN `tv_thelook.inventory_items` AS i ON i.id = oi.inventory_item_id AND i.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN `tv_thelook.products` AS sold ON sold.id = i.product_id
JOIN `tv_thelook.products` AS reported ON reported.id = oi.id
WHERE oi.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND oi.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND sold.category IS DISTINCT FROM reported.category
GROUP BY sold_category, report_category
ORDER BY affected_lines DESC, sold_category ASC, report_category ASC
LIMIT 20

rubric: The inventory unit and order line agree on the sold product, so sold.category identifies its catalog category.
The report looks up the order-line ID as a catalog ID. An incidental match can yield a different category. The correct report join is p.id = oi.product_id.

item.complaint:
The three counts in the February summary add up to 231. Before I book that as the completed-order subtotal, which column in this reconciliation should equal 231? I kept the three reported dates fixed.

SELECT COUNT(*) AS all_shipments,
  COUNTIF(o.status = 'Complete') AS complete_shipments
FROM `tv_thelook.orders` AS o
WHERE o.shipped_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND o.shipped_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND DATE(o.shipped_at, 'UTC') IN (DATE '2025-02-11', DATE '2025-02-18', DATE '2025-02-24')
ORDER BY all_shipments DESC
LIMIT 1

rubric: all_shipments matches 231 on the three fixed UTC shipment dates because the report counts every order shipped on those dates.
Apply this missing predicate before grouping and ranking the dates. complete_shipments counts the qualifying subset on the fixed dates.

item.complaint:
A shipment can acquire a return timestamp after it goes out. When the summary calls February 11's 77 orders 'completed,' does that refer to their status at shipment or their recorded status when the report ran? I need to know whether a later return matters to that count.

SELECT o.status, COUNT(*) AS shipments,
  COUNTIF(o.returned_at > o.shipped_at) AS later_returns
FROM `tv_thelook.orders` AS o
WHERE o.shipped_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-11 00:00:00+00'
  AND o.shipped_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-02-12 00:00:00+00'
GROUP BY o.status
ORDER BY shipments DESC, o.status ASC
LIMIT 20

rubric: The 77 counts orders by o.shipped_at on February 11 UTC, across all statuses. A subsequent o.returned_at leaves the order in that count.
Adding this predicate would use the order status recorded when the query runs. The report contains no status-at-shipment test.

item.complaint:
Suppose a new browser first sent events on November 30 and logged enough that day to overtake Safari. Could it claim third place in your November report? This check isolates browsers with activity only on the final day of that month.

SELECT e.browser, COUNT(*) AS november_events
FROM `tv_thelook.events` AS e
WHERE e.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND e.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND e.browser IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY e.browser
HAVING MIN(e.created_at) >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-30 00:00:00+00'
ORDER BY november_events DESC, e.browser ASC
LIMIT 10

rubric: A browser active only on November 30 has no qualifying rows and cannot enter the reported top three, regardless of that day's event count.
With the full month included, its November 30 events count toward its rank against every other browser's full-month total.

item.complaint:
If one February 24 order changes from Complete to Returned in my test copy, should the reported 73 drop to 72? Its shipment timestamp stays the same. This is the count I would expect to fall by one.

SELECT COUNT(*) AS complete_shipments
FROM `tv_thelook.orders` AS o
WHERE o.status = 'Complete'
  AND o.shipped_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-24 00:00:00+00'
  AND o.shipped_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-02-25 00:00:00+00'
ORDER BY complete_shipments DESC
LIMIT 1

rubric: With o.shipped_at unchanged, the order still contributes to February 24 and the reported count stays 73.
The report omits this predicate. Changing one order from Complete to Returned lowers the Complete-only check by one from its own starting count.

item.complaint:
I'm handing off the centers that received stock from 08:00 to 09:00 UTC and then went quiet for the next hour. Why would those centers drop out of the 09:00 ranking just when I need to see them?

SELECT dc.id AS center_id,
  COUNTIF(i.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-05-14 09:00:00+00') AS first_hour_units,
  COUNTIF(i.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-14 09:00:00+00') AS second_hour_units
FROM `tv_thelook.distribution_centers` AS dc
JOIN `tv_thelook.inventory_items` AS i ON i.product_distribution_center_id = dc.id
WHERE i.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-05-14 08:00:00+00'
  AND i.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-05-14 10:00:00+00'
GROUP BY dc.id
HAVING first_hour_units > 0 AND second_hour_units = 0
ORDER BY first_hour_units DESC, center_id ASC
LIMIT 20

rubric: Receipts from 08:00 to 09:00 UTC fall outside the report hour. A center quiet from 09:00 to 10:00 has no row in receipts, so the inner join drops it.
Starting from the center roster lets COALESCE(r.units_received, 0) assign zero and makes the quiet center eligible for the five-fewest ranking.

item.complaint:
I'm reconciling the February 11 shipment count to our hourly log. An hour can show shipments even when the Complete column is zero. Does that hour add anything to the 77 in the daily summary?

SELECT TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(o.shipped_at, HOUR, 'UTC') AS ship_hour,
  COUNT(*) AS shipments, COUNTIF(o.status = 'Complete') AS complete_shipments
FROM `tv_thelook.orders` AS o
WHERE o.shipped_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-11 00:00:00+00'
  AND o.shipped_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-02-12 00:00:00+00'
GROUP BY ship_hour
ORDER BY ship_hour ASC
LIMIT 24

rubric: Every shipment in the hour contributes to the reported February 11 count of 77, even when complete_shipments is zero.
The report omits this filter. With it, that hour contributes zero to the daily Complete shipment count.
